RFC7752-3.1-1.note: D2 rejudge 2026-10-16 (independent judge, BGP-LS codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/bgpls). Tagged units changed only by the package move: identifiers re-qualified with bgpls., comments re-pointed; producer bodies byte-identical modulo the writeTLV->WriteTLV and field-export renames (TLV code constants verified unchanged). RFC 7752 Section 3.1: "Unrecognized types MUST be preserved and propagated." Proof is carried by reactor TestRFC7752UnknownTLVsReachForwardDestinations (exact forwarded NLRI and attribute bytes, internal and external peers, all-unknown attribute variant). The ls unit now calls bgpls.ParseBGPLSWithRest and additionally requires the one NLRI to consume the whole buffer (a strengthening); it keeps the opaque attribute TLV under a generic key and re-encodes the Node NLRI byte-identically.

RFC7752-3.1-2.note: D2 rejudge 2026-10-16 (independent judge, BGP-LS codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/bgpls). Tagged units changed only by the package move: identifiers re-qualified with bgpls., comments re-pointed; producer bodies byte-identical modulo the writeTLV->WriteTLV and field-export renames (TLV code constants verified unchanged). RFC 7752 Section 3.1: "In order to compare NLRIs with unknown TLVs, all TLVs MUST be ordered in ascending order by TLV Type." The core units (internal/core/bgp/nlri/bgpls/rfc9552_ordering_test.go) are byte-identical to the deleted plugin copies apart from the package clause: mixed-family Link Descriptor emits 260 before 261, and the sweep over link/node/prefix descriptors finds no descending pair. The native whole-NLRI proof stays with ls_export encodeNativeLink (canonical and reordered-source units). Note the negative is a sweep of the sender, not a rejected input; the ordering duty is the originator's.

RFC7752-3.1-3.note: rejudge 2026-09-30 (was wrong: the tagged 518 units asserted the RFC 9552 Length-first rule; tags removed under D-15). Now the ls_export units assert same-type 259/260/261/262 ascending by Value compared leftmost octet first, from ascending and descending sources. Every Type this producer repeats has one fixed Length, so the 'regardless of the length' comparison and RFC 9552's Length-then-Value order give identical output; judge break (Value comparison reversed) turns both red.

RFC7752-3.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c31 judge) after the send path was tagged here. RFC 7752 Section 3.2: "In order for two BGP speakers to exchange Link-State NLRI, they MUST use BGP Capabilities Advertisement to ensure that they are both capable of properly processing such NLRI." reactor rfc9552_capability_test.go::TestRFC9552LinkStateSentToCapablePeer drives AnnounceNLRIBatch to an established peer that negotiated (16388, 71) and asserts one UPDATE whose MP_REACH_NLRI starts 40 04 47; ::TestRFC9552LinkStateNeverSentToIncapablePeer drives the same NLRI to an IPv4-unicast-only peer and asserts no UPDATE written and ErrNoPeersAcceptedFamily. The HEAD capability units keep the advertisement and the Negotiate intersection (unrecorded). Judge overlay: the per-peer gate `nc == nil || !nc.Has(batch.Family)` reduced to `nc == nil` turns the negative red and leaves the positive green; revert records exist on both new units. Row is superseded by RFC9552-5.2-7, whose verdict rests on the same two units. Receive side (an unnegotiated peer sending Link-State NLRI) is not driven, as on RFC9552-5.2-7; the sentence obliges the speaker to gate the exchange on the capability, which the send-path pair proves.

RFC7752-3.2-4.note: Forbidden: merging NLRIs that differ only in Identifier. TestRFC7752DifferentIdentifierIsDifferentRoutingUniverse inserts two Node NLRIs identical except Identifier 0 and 1 and fails unless rib.Len() is 2, both are retrievable, and removing one leaves the other. Negative: TestRFC7752SameIdentifierIsOneRoutingUniverse fails unless a repeat with the same Identifier collapses to one route (Len 1), so the separation turns on the Identifier bytes.

RFC7752-3.2.1.4-3.note: D2 rejudge 2026-10-16 (independent judge, BGP-LS codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/bgpls). Tagged units changed only by the package move: identifiers re-qualified with bgpls., comments re-pointed; producer bodies byte-identical modulo the writeTLV->WriteTLV and field-export renames (TLV code constants verified unchanged). RFC 7752 Section 3.2.1.4: "The sub-TLVs within a Node Descriptor MUST be arranged in ascending order by sub-TLV type." {single-polarity: positive} holds: TestRFC7752NodeDescriptorSubTLVsAscending fails unless bgpls.NodeDescriptor.WriteTo emits exactly 512..517 in order; that WriteTo is the production encoder (ls_export exportNodeID builds every native Node Descriptor through it, now via bgpls.NewBGPLSNode/Link/Prefix).

RFC7752-3.3.2.3-1.note: D2 rejudge 2026-10-16 (independent judge, BGP-LS codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/bgpls). Tagged units changed only by the package move: identifiers re-qualified with bgpls., comments re-pointed; producer bodies byte-identical modulo the writeTLV->WriteTLV and field-export renames (TLV code constants verified unchanged). RFC 7752 Section 3.3.2.3: "If a source protocol uses a metric width of less than 32 bits, then the high-order bits of this field MUST be padded with zero." Proof is the IS-IS pair (TestRFC7752TEDefaultMetricWidenedWithZeroHighOrder 0a0b0c->000a0b0c, TestRFC7752TEDefaultMetricAllOnesNeverReachesHighOrder ffffff->00ffffff) over the real producer isis bgpls_export. The plugin ls unit TestRFC7752TEDefaultMetricZeroPadded proves nothing about emitted bytes: lsTEDefaultMetric is constructed only by its decoder and its WriteTo has no non-test caller; it is supplementary and earns no credit.

RFC7752-3.3.2.7-1.note: D2 rejudge 2026-10-16 (independent judge, BGP-LS codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/bgpls). Cited producer originateAttributes changed only by ls.WriteTLVBytes -> bgpls.WriteTLVBytes. RFC 7752 Section 3.3.2.7: "The use of FQDN or a subset of it is strongly RECOMMENDED." No native naming policy exists: originateAttributes copies supplied TLV values (sorted, reserved-cleared) and decodeLinkName decodes a received string. Optional implementation gap, not a rejection duty.

RFC7752-3.4-1.note: {single-polarity: positive} carried on the row. Forbidden: a BGP-LS MP_REACH_NLRI whose next hop departs from the RFC 4760 layout. TestRFC7752BGPLSNextHopFollowsRFC4760 fails unless, for AFI 16388 SAFI 71, the encoder emits AFI, SAFI, next-hop length 4 or 16, the address, a zero reserved octet and then the NLRI, and the parse round-trips; IPv4 and IPv6 next hops both asserted.
